summary: The link that carries piston force to the crank pin and turns the reciprocating motion into rotation.

variants.name: Master rod with four link rods on slipper shoes
variants.applies_to: Five-cylinder radial on a single crank pin (Langley / Manly-Balzer)
distinguishing_features: one master rod with an integral sleeve half carries the crank-pin load
four link rods end in bronze slipper shoes that slide on the master sleeve
7/8 in rods, link rods with a 5/8 in hole
split bronze lining on the crank pin

dimensions.name: crank radius
dimensions.basis: Half the documented stroke of 5.5 in (A1 p. 156).

dimensions.name: rod length, gudgeon axis to crank pin axis
dimensions.basis: Not documented. Bounded by shoe clearance (about 278 mm for 55 degree shoes) and the 37 in overall diameter (part-spec.json rod_length).

dimensions.name: shoe angular width
dimensions.basis: M1 p. 237 says "slightly less than sixty degrees"; adjacent rods approach to 55.6 degrees at the modelled proportions (part-spec.json shoe_angular_width).

construction.note: Upper sleeve half, integral with the rod, from a derived profile
Little end with a cone neck; cut a bore for the gudgeon pin
Link rod: 7/8 in tube with a 5/8 in hole, little end, cone neck
Bronze slipper shoe as an arc of the sleeve radius, plus a boss

function.role: Carry piston load into one shared crank pin: the master rod directly, the link rods through shoes that slide on the master sleeve.
function.motion: The master rod swings with the crank pin; each link rod swings about its own gudgeon pin while its shoe slides on the master sleeve.

envelope.statement: Adjacent link rods are 72 degrees apart and approach each other as they swing, so shoe width and rod length are bounded together.
The 37 in overall engine diameter bounds the rod length from above.
envelope.basis: part-spec.json rod_length rationale; A1 p. 156 gives the diameter.

intent.statement: Master-and-link rods let all five pistons work on one crank pin, which makes a radial engine with a single throw possible.
intent.basis: Standard function of the arrangement; inventory L05 and L06 record it (M1 pp. 237-238) without stating the purpose.

manufacturing.material: steel rods and sleeve, bronze shoes and lining
manufacturing.process: forged rod with integral sleeve half; bronze shoes and split lining

instances.validation: Interference audit of the exported file is clean: 1,492 neighbouring pairs at rest, 133 poses of the baked clip, 0 overlaps (interference-audit.json); mass check against the Memoir weight table in build-notes.md.

gaps: Rod length is not documented: the Plate 78 fold-out hides the strip that would measure it.
How the halves of the master sleeve are held together is not drawn clearly enough to state (inventory L05).
Model mass of the rod group is 1.45 times the weight table line W02 (7,366 g against 5,070 g): unresolved (build-notes.md).

variants.name: Three-piece rod: steel tube with threaded bronze ends
variants.applies_to: Four-cylinder water-cooled engine with one crank throw per cylinder (Wright 1903)
distinguishing_features: separate phosphor-bronze big end with a split cap
separate bronze little end with a clamp
direct threaded joints held by retaining pins

dimensions.name: rod length
dimensions.basis: Teaching dimension in part-spec.json (rod_length); not a transcribed production dimension.

dimensions.name: tube outer diameter
dimensions.basis: RodTube1 feature radius 8 mm in part-spec.json.

dimensions.name: tube bore
dimensions.basis: RodTube1 feature inner radius 5 mm in part-spec.json.

dimensions.name: rod count
dimensions.basis: One rod per cylinder; the study specifies four cylinders (part-spec.json cylinders, sources H1 and L1).

dimensions.name: crank radius
dimensions.basis: Half the documented stroke of 4 in (H1 pp. 10-11).

construction.note: Seamless steel tube; cut seats for the two retaining pins
Big end: bearing boss and block, bored for the journal
Big end split cap face; cut a thread engagement socket and seats for bolts and shim
Little end: annulus and boss, bored for the wrist pin
Little-end clamp split; cut a thread engagement socket

function.role: Transmit the reversing load between the wrist pin and the crank journal.
function.motion: Swings with the crank: the big end turns on the journal, the little end oscillates on the wrist pin.

envelope.statement: The joints are the Science Museum direct-thread type, steel tube into bronze ends; the Smithsonian adapter and brazed route is excluded.
Rod swing is about 12 degrees either side of the axis.
envelope.basis: asin(crank radius 50.8 mm / rod length 245 mm) = 11.97 degrees; rod length is inferred, so the swing is inferred too.

intent.statement: A thin steel tube with bronze ends puts the bearing metal only where it runs on a shaft or pin and keeps the rod light.
intent.basis: Read from the construction recorded in inventory S03; no source in the study states the reason.

manufacturing.process: threaded tube-to-end joints with retaining pins

instances.validation: Interference audit of the exported file is clean: 1,121 neighbouring pairs at rest, 133 poses of the baked clip, 0 overlaps (interference-audit.json); geometry is valid but historical accuracy is not verified (cad-validation.json).

gaps: Thread fits and attachment sizes are estimates.
Rod length is a teaching dimension, so the swing angle is not a documented value.
